yearMeaning: First modern Czech observance in 2001; 2004 is the year 11 November became a Czech legally recognized significant day, distinct from the 1918 armistice.
authority: Czech Republic; Ministry of Defence and Czech significant-day legislation
dateReason: 11 November 1918 armistice on the Western Front, observed annually in remembrance of veterans.

sourceEvidence.claim: Czech Armed Forces history: armistice in 1918, Czech commemoration from 2001 and statutory significant-day recognition from 2004.
Czech Defence Ministry Military History Institute: first Czech remembrance at Vítkov in 2001; law 170/2002 and poppy symbolism.
Czech Ministry of Defence report dated 11 November 2026 confirms official observance since 2004.

narratives.en: On 11 November, Czechia honours war veterans, linking national remembrance to the armistice that halted fighting on the Western Front in 1918. Czech commemorations began in 2001, with a ceremony at Prague's Vítkov memorial. The date became a legally recognized significant day in 2004. The red poppy recalls those killed in war, while today's observance also recognizes surviving veterans and people who served in later overseas operations. The 1918 armistice, the 2001 Czech commemoration and the 2004 statutory recognition are separate milestones.
narratives.it: L'11 novembre la Repubblica Ceca rende omaggio ai veterani di guerra, collegando la memoria nazionale all'armistizio che fermò i combattimenti sul fronte occidentale nel 1918. Le commemorazioni ceche iniziarono nel 2001, con una cerimonia al memoriale di Vítkov a Praga. Nel 2004 la data entrò tra le giornate significative riconosciute dalla legge. Il papavero rosso ricorda i caduti, mentre oggi si onorano anche i veterani viventi e coloro che hanno prestato servizio in missioni all'estero. L'armistizio del 1918, la prima commemorazione ceca del 2001 e il riconoscimento del 2004 sono tappe distinte.
narratives.es: El 11 de noviembre, Chequia rinde homenaje a los veteranos de guerra y vincula su memoria nacional con el armisticio que detuvo los combates en el frente occidental en 1918. Las conmemoraciones checas comenzaron en 2001 con una ceremonia en el monumento de Vítkov, en Praga. En 2004 la fecha pasó a ser un día significativo reconocido por ley. La amapola roja recuerda a los caídos, mientras que la jornada también reconoce a los veteranos vivos y a quienes sirvieron en misiones posteriores en el extranjero. El armisticio de 1918, la primera conmemoración checa de 2001 y el reconocimiento de 2004 son hitos diferentes.
narratives.fr: Le 11 novembre, la Tchéquie rend hommage aux anciens combattants, en reliant la mémoire nationale à l'armistice qui mit fin aux combats sur le front occidental en 1918. Les commémorations tchèques débutèrent en 2001, lors d'une cérémonie au mémorial de Vítkov à Prague. En 2004, la date fut inscrite parmi les journées importantes reconnues par la loi. Le coquelicot rouge rappelle les morts de guerre; la journée honore également les vétérans encore en vie et les personnes engagées dans des opérations extérieures plus récentes. L'armistice de 1918, la première commémoration de 2001 et la reconnaissance de 2004 sont trois étapes distinctes.
narratives.de: Am 11. November ehrt Tschechien seine Kriegsveteranen und verbindet das nationale Gedenken mit dem Waffenstillstand, der 1918 die Kämpfe an der Westfront beendete. Die tschechischen Gedenkveranstaltungen begannen 2001 mit einer Zeremonie am Vítkov-Denkmal in Prag. Seit 2004 zählt das Datum zu den gesetzlich anerkannten bedeutenden Tagen. Die rote Mohnblume erinnert an die Kriegstoten; zugleich werden lebende Veteranen und Angehörige späterer Auslandseinsätze gewürdigt. Der Waffenstillstand von 1918, das erste tschechische Gedenken 2001 und die gesetzliche Anerkennung 2004 sind unterschiedliche historische Stationen.
narratives.pt: A 11 de novembro, a Chéquia homenageia os veteranos de guerra, associando a memória nacional ao armistício que interrompeu os combates na frente ocidental em 1918. As comemorações checas começaram em 2001, com uma cerimónia no memorial de Vítkov, em Praga. Em 2004, a data passou a integrar os dias significativos reconhecidos por lei. A papoila vermelha recorda os mortos em guerra, enquanto a celebração também homenageia veteranos vivos e quem participou em operações posteriores no estrangeiro. O armistício de 1918, a primeira comemoração checa em 2001 e o reconhecimento de 2004 são marcos distintos.
